subject: error using refresh to silence cmdstan output

messages.author: b71a113cd1f5d048
messages.subject: error using refresh to silence cmdstan output
parts:
Hi All,

I'm using cmdstan 2.1.0 (OS X 10.9.1) and I want to inhibit output to the terminal (from multiple chains in parallel). I followed the Sampling in Parallel subsubsection of subsection 4.1 of the Stan Modeling Language and tried to set refresh=0, but I get the following error (same for each chain):


0 is not a valid value for "refresh"
Valid values: 0 < refresh
Failed to parse arguments, terminating Stan

Here's the for loop I used to start multiple chains (from bash shell file):

for i in {1..3}; do
./preemulator method=sample \
num_samples=1000 \
num_warmup=1000 \
save_warmup=1 \
thin=1 \
data file=$1.data.R \
random seed=100$i \
output file=$1.out$i.csv refresh=0 \
id=$i &
done

This works fine if refresh is a positive integer. I saw some posts wherein refresh=-1, but that didn't work either.

Best,

Jarrett

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] error using refresh to silence cmdstan output
parts:
Sorry about that.

It's a known issue that refresh=0 is broken:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/427?source=cc

Thanks for pointing out where the manual's also broken.

I'll update the manual before the next release because I don't
think we'll get to fixing refresh=0 before our next release,
which is imminent. Here's the issue tracking the
manual fixes:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/485?source=cc

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] error using refresh to silence cmdstan output
parts:
To get rid of all the output, you'd ned to redirect the
standard output to /dev/null, as in:

$ ./normal sample output > /dev/null
$

Or you can choose a very high refresh rate (greater than num_samples + num_warmup),
but you'll still get the output of the configuration, the first
iteration, first sampling iteration, and last sampling iteration.

- Bob
